/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 08 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2978 (-56)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4955 (-184)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2233 (38)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1522 (1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 833 (6)
CAPESIZE
The market took a breather today, with sentiment softening across both basins after the strong gains seen earlier in the week. Following such rapid upward momentum, today’s correction felt more like a reassessment of levels rather than a collapse in underlying fundamentals. The BCI 182 5TC declined by $1,669 to settle at $44,910. In the Pacific, activity remained relatively healthy with two major miners active on C5, although sentiment weakened as the day progressed. Offers reportedly started the morning in the low $16s before slipping into the high-to-mid $15s, reflecting a more cautious tone. Bids initially opened around $14.50, with $14.85 eventually fixed before later reports emerged closer to $15.30. Ultimately, C5 eased by $0.515 to close at $15.20.
The Atlantic also softened, particularly on South Brazil and West Africa to China, where the week ended quietly. Spreads narrowed considerably following a couple of softer C3 fixtures reported overnight at $35.50 for 10–15 June laycans, contributing to C3 falling $1.296 to $35.509. The North Atlantic appeared comparatively more resilient, with brokers indicating trading levels around $46,000 versus previous indications nearer $51,000. On the period front OTSL is reported to have fixed the Trident controlled Bulk Harvest (175,617 2012) delivery Mailiao 18/20 May for a one year timecharter at $31,000.
PANAMAX
The week wrapped up on a firm footing with optimism continuing across both the Atlantic and Pacific regions as the P5TC rose by $341 to close at $20,099. Activity picked up in the Atlantic, with brokers noting a rise in cargo availability and a higher number of concluded fixtures compared to the previous days. Some participants highlighted a gap in rate levels between longer and shorter voyages, as charterers are having to incentivise owners to commit to shorter trips. Available tonnage is reportedly tightening, impacting both the transatlantic and fronthaul markets while reported grain fronthaul fixtures continue to show solid volumes. In Asia, the week drew to a slightly calmer close, though overall sentiment remains positive. Brokers observed an increase in cargo volume from the North Pacific, while mineral shipments from Australia and Indonesia continue to build on the momentum seen earlier in the week. Messrs Fullinks were linked to the Guo Yuan 10 (75,980 2011) open in Mariveles 12/13 May fixing for a trip via Indonesia to South China with coal at $24,250, although some brokers suggested this may be a trip via East Coast Australia into India.
SUPRAMAX
It was unsurprisingly a rather lacklustre end to the week, although relatively speaking brokers said rates generally remained fairly healthy. In the Atlantic, the US Gulf was still described as positional and in the South Atlantic some spoke of support for fronthaul business although no fixture information surfaced. Fundamentals changed little from the Asian arena, although some felt a ceiling had been reached from the south. Period activity was limited throughout the week, but a newbuilding ultramax was heard to have fixed ex yard China for 11 to 13 months period at $18,750, but no more details surfaced. The 11TC average finished the week up $14.00 from yesterday at $19,240.

Atlantic
The Christos K (63,197 2015) open St. Lawrence 15 May was heard to have been placed on subjects for a trip from Norfolk to the Continent with coal at $24,000. Also, the Berge Rysy (63,923 2025) open New Orleans mid May was said to have been fixed basis delivery SW Pass trip West Mediterranean with corn at $28,000 to Navimerchants.

Asia
The AM Ocean Pearl (56,819 2011) open Koh Sichang 7/12 May was placed on subjects at $13,000 for an Indonesia to China run with coal, but no more details came to light.
HANDYSIZE
The week concluded on a generally positive note, with continued optimism expected across both the Atlantic and Pacific basins. The BHSI rose by 6 points to reach 833, while the 7TC settled at $14,994. Markets in the South Atlantic and US Gulf remained steady and positive, with fundamentals showing little fluctuation and maintaining stability throughout the week. The Continent and Mediterranean regions experienced a quieter day, with sentiment remaining flat as rates edged slightly lower. In contrast, the Asian market continued its upward momentum. Participants remained cautiously optimistic as rates strengthened further, supporting an overall positive outlook for the region.

Atlantic
The Negmar Meko (38,656 2013), open in Aliaga, was fixed on voyage terms from the Black Sea to the US West Coast, although no additional details were disclosed. Additionally, a 40,000 was rumored fixed for a trip from Recalada to Morocco at approximately $25,000 - $26,000, but further specifics were not available.

Asia
A 38,000 was reportedly fixed for a trip from Yangzhou to Indonesia at $17,500. However, no further information was confirmed regarding this fixture.

ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih Announces Part Shutdown
ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih based in Ukraine has halted parts of
its mining and steel production facilities as wartime logistics
disruptions, soaring electricity costs, and weakening export
access continue to pressure Ukraine’s steel sector, newswires
report. This comes following a statement by the company
earlier this year announcing the closure of one of its
production units in the second quarter. The company cited
bottlenecks in rail and port logistics alongside rising energy
tariﬀs and the EU’s CBAM carbon border rules, which have
reduced competitiveness in European markets. Production
cuts at rolling and blooming mills are expected to weigh on
Ukrainian steel output and exports, while highlighting the
broader operational strain facing heavy industry during the
ongoing conﬂict.
Brazilian Corn Exports
Brazil’s corn exports dipped halved from the prior month to
0.5 Mt in April, although rose 0.3 Mt year-on-year, full month
oﬃcial data released on 7 May show. The majority of these
shipments were destined to Iran (ﬂat year-on-year at 0.13
Mt), while exports to Viet Nam and Egypt both lifted 0.1 Mt
on the year to 0.1 Mt each. According to a report by S&P
Global, Iran’s buying activity lifted in April following a
relatively subdued start to the year due to geopolitical and
payment-related uncertainties. Iran was the top export
destination for Brazil’s corn in CY2025, making up ~22% of
exports at 9.1 Mt.

Ship owners, encouraged by continuing strong freight earnings, are electing to
trade their ageing tonnage for longer periods, further postponing recycling
decisions during what many perceive to be an unexpected window of oppor-
tunity. Consequently, only a total of 105 vessels, equating to approximately
3.3 million dwt and close to 800,000 lwt, have reportedly been sold for recy-
cling during the first four months of the year.

The past week has once again seen a number of previously unreported sales
subsequently arriving at their final destinations. In terms of fresh business, we
are able to report the sale of the bulk carrier “Jenny Lucky” (7,176 lwt), which
has been committed to Pakistan at a reported level of USD 450 per lwt. The
small tanker “Xiang Hai” (2,402 lwt) has also arrived in Gadani following her
earlier sale on private terms.

At the Bangladesh anchorage, it is noted that the bulk carrier
“Festival” (7,125 lwt) and the container vessel “Spruce” (2,217 lwt) have both
recently arrived and delivered.

Despite the recent improvement seen from Bangladesh over the past few
weeks, pricing has softened slightly during the course of the last few days,
largely due to the immediate demand from the waterfront now having been
satisfied following the recent influx of tonnage. Even so, underlying sentiment
remains comparatively firm by recent standards.

Enquiry from ship recyclers remains healthy across all major destinations;
however, the continuing shortage of available tonnage remains the principal
obstacle in satisfying demand from the waterfront. While domestic steel mar-
kets softened slightly over the course of the past week, this has not materially
impacted the pricing levels currently being offered by recyclers.

India, in pricing terms, continues to lag behind both Bangladesh and Pakistan,
although a noticeable increase in enquiry is beginning to emerge from this
sector. India’s strength continues to lie in specialised and HKC -compliant ton-
nage, with buyers remaining particularly active for vessels containing higher
quantities of stainless steel or non -ferrous material.

Looking ahead, market fundamentals remain broadly supportive despite the
shortage of available candidates. With recyclers continuing to show underlying
appetite and many HKC -compliant yards actively competing for tonnage, there
remains cautious optimism that pricing could remain firm, particularly should
freight markets soften or operating costs begin to pressure older vessels later
in the year.

Brazil’s Clean Product Imports Fall To Eight -Month Low
Brazil’s clean oil product imports declined by 20K b/d m -o-m and by 60K b/d y -o-y to 370K b/d in April, an eight -month low, acco rd-
ing to data from Brazil’s trade ministry. Diesel arrivals increased by 40K b/d m -o-m to 250K b/d. Meanwhile, gasoline and naphth a
shipments decreased by 10K b/d m -o-m to 50K b/d and by 30K b/d m -o-m to 60K b/d respectively.

ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih Announces Part Shutdown
ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih based in Ukraine has halted parts of its mining and steel production facilities as wartime logistics disrup-
tions, soaring electricity costs, and weakening export access continue to pressure Ukraine’s steel sector, newswires report. This
comes following a statement by the company earlier this year announcing the closure of one of its production units in the sec ond
quarter. The company cited bottlenecks in rail and port logistics alongside rising energy tariffs and the EU’s CBAM carbon bo rder
rules, which have reduced competitiveness in European markets. Production cuts at rolling and blooming mills are expected to weigh
on Ukrainian steel output and exports, while highlighting the broader operational strain facing heavy industry during the ong oing con-
flict.

Brazilian Corn Exports
Brazil’s corn exports dipped halved from the prior month to 0.5 Mt in April, although rose 0.3 Mt year -on-year, full month offic ial data
released on 7 May show. The majority of these shipments were destined to Iran (flat year -on-year at 0.13 Mt), while exports to V iet
Nam and Egypt both lifted 0.1 Mt on the year to 0.1 Mt each. According to a report by S&P Global, Iran’s buying activity lift ed in April
following a relatively subdued start to the year due to geopolitical and payment -related uncertainties. Iran was the top export destina-
tion for Brazil’s corn in CY2025, making up ~22% of exports at 9.1 Mt.

This comes following a statement by the company earlier this year announcing the closure of one of its production units in the second quarter. The company cited bottlenecks in rail and port logistics alongside rising energy tariffs and the EU’s CBAM carbon border rules, which have reduced competitiveness in European markets. Production cuts at rolling and blooming mills are expected to weigh on Ukrainian steel output and exports, while highlighting the broader operational strain facing heavy industry during the ongoing conflict. Brazilian Corn Exports Brazil’s corn exports dipped halved from the prior month to 0.5 Mt in April, although rose 0.3 Mt year-on-year, full month oﬃcial data released on 7 May show. The majority of these shipments were destined to Iran (flat year-on-year at 0.13 Mt), while exports to Viet Nam and Egypt both lifted 0.1 Mt on the year to 0.1 Mt each. According to a report by S&P Global, Iran’s buying activity lifted in April following a relatively subdued start to the year due to geopolitical and payment-related uncertainties. Iran was the top export destination for Brazil’s corn in CY2025, making up ~22% of exports at 9.1 Mt.
